questions.text: Which scenario best fits A2A’s delegation model as taught in this lesson?

options.A: Calling a specific arithmetic function with two numeric arguments.
options.B: Reading a known document from a resource URI.
options.C: Delegating report writing to another agent while observing task state and artifacts.
options.D: Sharing both agents’ internal reasoning and tool traces as a required protocol step.

questions.explanation: A2A supports task delegation between agents whose internal implementations remain opaque, with task lifecycle and artifacts as the visible contract.

questions.text: The writer task pauses with TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED to ask for targetLength. How does the lesson’s caller resume that same task?

options.A: Send a new message carrying the existing taskId and a data part with targetLength.
options.B: Create a new task without taskId and assume the writer merges it automatically.
options.C: Change the Agent Card’s defaultOutputModes to the desired length.
options.D: Mark the task completed locally and read its empty artifact list.

questions.explanation: The follow-up supplies the missing value in a data part and carries the existing taskId, allowing the writer to retrieve and continue that task.

questions.text: What does part_content({"text":"hello", "data":{"targetLength":"short"}}) do in the supplied harness?

options.A: It returns text because text is first in PART_CONTENT_FIELDS.
options.B: It returns data because structured input takes precedence.
options.C: It merges both values into one valid message part.
options.D: It raises ValueError because two content fields are present.

questions.explanation: part_content collects every present content field and requires exactly one; two fields trigger ValueError.
